messages:
maya: FYI: noticed a ~24% small-seq tail latency regression on master after the cuDNN/Driver bump + torch2.4 merge. CI nightly flagged it.
ci-bot: nightly-perf-check: latency_regression=+24% (p95 small-seq, model=redwood/gpt-small), build=master-2026-09-14
jonathan: link to perf logs? can you paste perf summary + GPU profile?
maya: pasted perf summary & nvprof snippet
maya: ```
perf_summary:
 p50: 12.6ms -> 15.6ms
 p95: 28.0ms -> 34.7ms
 tokens/sec: 800 -> 620
commit: 8f3a2b torch2.4/cuDNN-9.1 driver 531.41
```
sanjay: interesting, KV cache memcpy time jumped. I see a lot more cudaMemset/cudaMalloc activity in the profile. Could be allocator behavior with cuMemAllocAsync.
lina: also saw a different matmul kernel being picked in the new Triton kernels for sm_80, plus changed workspace sizes.
jonathan: can we bisect range? suspecting either torch2.4 merge or driver bump. maya can you run a quick local bisect with our perf harness?
maya: started bisect: `git bisect start -- bad master -- good v2.3.8` running on a100-prod-sim with minimal trace. Reproducer command:
maya: ```
./scripts/run_small_seq_perf.sh --model gpt-small --seq 32 --batch 1 --iters 200 --trace=nvtx
```
ash: observed same locally, pinned driver back to 530.* and regression disappears. So driver is hot suspect.
sanjay: pinned torch2.4? try reverting the Triton bump in the runtime branch too, we saw kernel selection changes there.
maya: did a quick bisect: reverting triton->2.0.1 made p95 go back ~8%. reverting driver back to 530 made it go back ~23%. So driver bump is larger effect.
jonathan: interesting — could be new cuBLAS kernel selection or different workspace-algo causing extra allocations. can you dump kernel names used (cublasSelector) from the runtime logs?
maya: attached runtime_excerpt.log (pasted snippet)
maya: ```
[2026-09-14 12:03:22] kernel_select: matmul_algo=cublasLt_fmha_1 workspace=0.5MB
[2026-09-14 12:03:22] kernel_select: matmul_algo=cublasLt_fmha_3 workspace=4MB
KV::prefetch memcpy: 0.47ms -> 1.9ms
```
lina: the workspace increase could push more allocations into async allocator fallback paths; cuMemAllocAsync fragmentation still different on new driver.
jonathan: work to do: 1) reproduce in controlled env with mem-trace 2) try cuMemAllocAsync tunables (arena sizes) 3) add telemetry for kernel names and workspace sizes to console
maya: opened internal ticket INF-4821 and added perf logs + bisect notes. tagging @eng-sre for rollout hold.
sanjay: quick mitigation: force-select older cublas kernel fallback in runtime for sm_80 when seq<=32 (cheap flag). Patch PR up next.
ci-bot: deploy-blocker: rollout-onhold=INF-4821
ash: thanks — will validate the runtime patch on canary and run nightly perf. :thumbsup:
maya: If canary looks good, we'll revert driver pin for next release, and file vendor bug to NV driver team. Adding triage notes to RFC.
jonathan: one more note — also saw increased CPU-side scheduling while memcpy waits; might need to offload some work to streams to overlap better.
lina: adding an experiment to TuneAllocator pipeline to expand arenas for small-alloc workloads.
maya: ok, will follow up with numbers tomorrow. thx all.
ci-bot: thread closed for now (but will reopen if nightly fails)
